description: Primary-source additions for Switzerland’s THG proposal, Norway’s battery-registry consultation and Taiwan’s resource-circulation law and voluntary DPP pilot.

relationship_definitions.references: An explicit source reference or contextual discussion; it does not establish legal incorporation, conformity, standard adoption or mutual recognition.
relationship_definitions.part_of: A provision identified within its named legal instrument; implementation scope and dates remain qualified in the records.

entities.label: Swiss THG proposal: digital product information system
entities.description: The June 2026 consultation draft would authorise a digital product information system, with sector decisions and compatibility with trading-partner systems considered separately.

status.scope_note: Consultation closed on 28 September 2026. The reviewed proposal is not an enacted Swiss DPP requirement.

limitations: The consultation announcement and explanatory report do not establish subsequent enactment or a mandatory DPP for any product category.
A domestic system or participation in a trading-partner system remains an option; no mutual recognition or completed interoperability is established.

entities.label: Norway battery regulation consultation: passport registry
entities.description: The Norwegian Environment Agency consulted on amendments to its proposed battery regulation, including the use of the product-passport registry for battery-passport identifiers.

status.scope_note: Consultation 2026/4456 closed on 11 May 2026. Subsequent adoption and current Norwegian applicability were not established by this source.

limitations: The source records a proposal and an expired consultation, not final enactment or EEA incorporation.
The source does not establish that the EU battery-passport application date already applies domestically in Norway.

entities.label: Taiwan
entities.description: Geographic join for the assessed Taiwanese legal framework and voluntary DPP pilot.

geography.join_note: TWN is used solely to join the assessed records to the existing map boundary dataset; the map is a geographic research index.

status.scope_note: Geographic research scope only; the presence of a record does not establish a universal DPP obligation.

entities.label: Taiwan Resource Circulation Promotion Act
entities.description: The amended Act establishes a resource-circulation framework including powers for product-information disclosure under Article 22.

status.scope_note: Amended on 17 June 2026. Article 52 brings the Act into force on promulgation, except Article 14 and Article 38(1), which take effect two years later.

dates.condition: Article 14 and Article 38(1), two years after promulgation.

limitations: The Act is an enabling framework; designated products, disclosure methods and deadlines require the relevant announcements and rules.
This record does not establish a general mandatory DPP rollout or a single DPP compliance date.
The official English translation states that the Chinese text prevails in case of discrepancy.

entities.label: Taiwan product-information disclosure: Article 22
entities.description: Article 22 enables designated products to carry material, repairability and circularity information; where a unique product code is used, traceability and quality-verification information must be updated.

status.scope_note: The authority must specify covered products, deadlines and methods. Products outside those designations may disclose information voluntarily.

dates.condition: Article 52; product-specific duties depend on implementing announcements.

limitations: No product-specific designation or implementing disclosure rule was verified for this update.
Article 22 does not itself prescribe W3C, UNTP or a particular DPP data model.

entities.label: Taiwan voluntary DPP pilot programme
entities.description: The Resource Circulation Administration reports a voluntary programme across batteries, textiles, ICT equipment and circular materials, alongside an open-source module and cross-border data-exchange testing.

status.scope_note: The 7 September 2026 agency report describes 28 participating companies and more than 20,000 product records. This is pilot evidence, not nationwide compliance.

limitations: Reported pilot results were not independently reproduced.
Cross-border tests do not establish formal mutual recognition, EU conformity or adoption of a named international technical standard.
The source places the pilot alongside Article 22 but does not establish a universal domestic DPP duty.

assertions.subject: global-ch-thg-dpp-proposal
assertions.statement: The Swiss explanatory report discusses the EU ESPR DPP framework when explaining the proposed Swiss product-information system.
assertions.locator: Draft Article 6b explanation, printed pages 19–20; explicit reference to EU Regulation 2024/1781
limitations: A reference to the EU framework does not establish Swiss incorporation, equivalence or mutual recognition.

assertions.subject: global-no-battery-registry-consultation
assertions.statement: The Norwegian consultation concerns amendments to the proposed national regulation implementing the EU Batteries Regulation.
limitations: This records the subject of a consultation, not final Norwegian implementation.

assertions.subject: global-no-battery-registry-consultation
assertions.statement: The consultation explicitly describes an amendment arising from the EU ecodesign regulation concerning product-passport registry use for battery-passport identifiers.
limitations: The proposed registry linkage does not prove that ESPR or the registry obligations are currently incorporated in Norwegian law.

assertions.subject: global-tw-product-information-art22
assertions.statement: Article 22 is a provision of Taiwan’s Resource Circulation Promotion Act.
limitations: Product-specific scope and deadlines are established through implementing announcements.

assertions.subject: global-tw-dpp-voluntary-pilot
assertions.statement: The Resource Circulation Administration’s pilot report identifies Article 22 as the legal framework for product-information disclosure while describing the voluntary DPP pilot.
assertions.locator: Paragraph connecting Article 22 to voluntary trials before implementation of the disclosure system
limitations: The agency report links the policy context and pilot; this does not make pilot participation mandatory.

assertions.subject: global-tw-dpp-voluntary-pilot
assertions.statement: The Taiwan pilot report discusses the EU battery-passport requirement as an international driver for supply-chain preparation.
assertions.locator: Paragraph on EU battery passports and the 18 February 2027 date
limitations: A reference to the EU requirement does not establish pilot conformity, legal recognition or adoption of an EU technical standard.
